source.title_on_document: Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback: Effects on creative problem-solving and feedback uptake

supplement.where: Included Appendix, PDF pp. 20-21 (printed pp. 184-185), Tables A1 and A2; referenced on PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), GenAI feedback conditions. No separate external supplement is identified.
supplement.holds: Table A1 describes personalisation settings and their roles; Table A2 gives representative prompts and personalised feedback examples. The appendix contains no additional outcome statistics or standard errors. Main condition-comparison means, SDs, Wilcoxon statistics, effect sizes and intervals are in Table 2 (PDF p. 11).

paper_design_summary: In an individual laboratory experiment, 62 Chinese university students completed product-improvement tasks using both standard ChatGPT-4 feedback and personalised Mr. Ranedeer feedback, with random assignment of feedback sequence (PDF pp. 4-5 and 8-9, Participants, Procedure and Figure 3). Two blinded trained raters scored their final solutions for quality, elaboration and originality while AI had been available during production (PDF pp. 7-8, Measures). The same sample also supplied conversation and screen-recording data for feedback-uptake and interaction analyses (PDF pp. 9-13).

studies.label: Laboratory crossover experiment: personalised versus standard GenAI feedback on product improvement

assignment.what_was_assigned: Feedback sequence: standard then personalised versus personalised then standard. Figure 3 explicitly labels random assignment and shows N = 31 in each sequence; both groups experience both GenAI conditions. The prose calls the design counterbalanced (PDF pp. 8-9, printed pp. 172-173).
assignment.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Figure 3, text inside the assignment box, verified in the rendered PDF; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure, for the laboratory setting and counterbalancing.

arms.name: Personalised GenAI feedback (Mr. Ranedeer)
arms.description: Mr. Ranedeer, based on GPT-4, uses learner preference configuration, a personalised learning plan, and adaptive feedback/scaffolding. All participants experience this condition in the crossover (PDF pp. 5-9, printed pp. 169-173; Figures 1-3). The 62 analyzed here are the same people as in the standard condition; randomisation was to sequence, not to an exclusive feedback arm.

arms.name: Standard GenAI feedback (ChatGPT-4)
arms.description: General-purpose ChatGPT-4 gives open-ended responses to general prompts, supporting unstructured exploration. All participants experience this condition in the crossover (PDF pp. 5-9, printed pp. 169-173; Figures 1-3). The 62 analyzed here are the same people as in the personalised condition; randomisation was to sequence, not to an exclusive feedback arm.

participants.exclusions: No exclusions, attrition, or larger recruitment count are stated. Participants reports a final sample of 62; Figure 3 shows 31 people in each of the two randomised sequences. The same 62 people contribute to both feedback conditions. No separate outcome-specific analyzed sample counts are given.
participants.who: Chinese university students from a normal university, with diverse academic majors and educational levels; 41 female; ages 18 to 27 years (M = 22.58, SD = 2.53). All but one reported prior GenAI experience (PDF pp. 4-5, printed pp. 168-169, Participants).
participants.quote: A total of 62 Chinese university students (41 female) from a normal university participated in the study.
participants.locator: PDF pp. 4-5 (printed pp. 168-169), Participants, including the explicit final sample size; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Figure 3, N = 31 on each randomised sequence branch. The total randomised count reflects those two branches, not two independent samples of 62.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4 and Mr. Ranedeer; both based on GPT-4 architecture (exact model snapshot/version not stated).
ai_tool.how_used: Participants freely entered prompts and adjusted their interactions with the assigned system via the web-based OpenAI interface. Standard ChatGPT-4 generated general feedback and ideas. Mr. Ranedeer used configured knowledge level, learning style, tone and communication style to create a personalised learning plan and provide dynamic scaffolding, heuristic questions, feedback and enhancement suggestions. It also supplied substantive content, so it was not a content-free coach (PDF pp. 5-8, printed pp. 169-172; Figures 1-2; Appendix Tables A1-A2, PDF pp. 20-21).

task.description: Torrance product improvement task (PIT): propose three original and useful improvement solutions for each of two everyday products, a stuffed bunny and a portable coffee maker, using the assigned GenAI tool. Final responses were submitted in Microsoft Word; instructions, materials and AI interactions were in Chinese (PDF p. 4, Participants; PDF pp. 7-8, Measures and Procedure; Figure 3 on PDF p. 9).
task.duration: Mean task completion time: standard condition 17 minutes (SD = 7), personalised condition 20 minutes (SD = 6), with a 5-minute break between tasks. No fixed time limit is stated (PDF p. 8, printed p. 172, Procedure).

outcomes.name: Solution quality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Quality refers to how well solutions addressed the task objectives. Two trained raters, blinded to experimental condition, independently rated all solutions on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = worst, 5 = best); solution presentation order was randomised and final scores were averaged across raters (PDF p. 8, printed p. 172, Measures: CPS performance). The paired condition comparison uses Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (PDF pp. 10-11, printed pp. 174-175, Data analysis and Table 2). The paper does not specify how the three solutions requested from each participant were combined into a condition score. The same outcome also appears in within-condition feedback-uptake correlations and regressions (PDF p. 12, printed p. 176, Tables 4-6); these are not additional randomised AI contrasts.

contrasts.reported: Standard mean (SD) = 3.08 (1.12); Personalised mean (SD) = 3.50 (1.00); Wilcoxon z = -3.24; p = .001; Cohen?s r = -0.41; 95% CI for Cohen?s r = [-0.607, -0.166].

eligibility.reason: Random assignment of within-person GenAI feedback sequence is explicit in Figure 3 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 173), and the experiment was conducted in a laboratory (PDF p. 8, Procedure). The final sample is 62 people, above the 50-person threshold (PDF pp. 4-5, Participants); they are counted once across the repeated conditions. Quality, elaboration and originality were rated on participants? product-improvement solutions by blinded raters (PDF pp. 7-8, Measures), with results in Table 2 (PDF p. 11). This is an ai_design comparison of two generative-AI configurations; AI was available during production in both conditions.

one_line_finding: Among 62 students in a laboratory crossover study, personalised versus standard GenAI feedback increased solution quality (3.50 vs 3.08, p = .001) and elaboration (3.58 vs 2.48, p < .001), with no clear originality difference (2.92 vs 3.13, p = 0.098; PDF p. 11, printed p. 175, Table 2; sample: PDF pp. 4-5, Participants).
open_questions: How were the three requested solutions per task aggregated into each participant?s Table 2 score? The paper explicitly states averaging across the two raters but does not specify aggregation across solutions (PDF pp. 7-8, Measures; PDF p. 11, Table 2).

The Procedure says the other sequence completed the tasks in the reverse order, whereas Figure 3 depicts PIT 1 followed by PIT 2 in both branches and reverses the feedback condition. Clarify product/task order if task-specific or order-effect extraction is needed (PDF pp. 8-9, Procedure and Figure 3).
notes: Screening completed from the entire markdown conversion, including references and appendix, with PDF verification of recorded numbers; all locators distinguish PDF page index plus one from printed journal page. Outcome inventory: Table 2 reports solution quality, elaboration and originality. Table 3 reports amount of ignored, copied, applied and total feedback. Tables 4-6 correlate/regress those same three CPS scores on feedback uptake; they do not introduce additional creative-output outcomes or randomised contrasts. Table 7 reports counts of generating ideas without interaction (CT1), building on GenAI ideas (CT2), developing ideas through interaction (CT3), personalised planning (TI1), task coordination/information (TI2), clarification requests (TI3), negotiating inconsistencies (TI4), irrelevant discourse (I), and total interactions. Figure 4 reports behavioural transitions and their adjusted residuals. These feedback-uptake and interaction measures describe the collaboration process, rather than creativity or diversity scores on the submitted products, and are not included as creative-output outcomes (PDF pp. 9-13, Coding scheme, Tables 1 and 3-7, Figure 4). Self-efficacy is a self-report covariate, not an output score (PDF pp. 8 and 10). Figures 1-2 illustrate system workflows and interfaces; Figure 3 documents assignment and procedure. Appendix Tables A1-A2 contain settings and feedback examples, with no additional outcome measures. All three included outcomes concern immediate work with AI available; no across-person diversity or unassisted after-AI outcome is reported. There is no aggregate overall-creativity score or explicitly designated primary outcome. The raters are described as trained, without stated domain-expert credentials, so human_raters is used. The task is coded divergent_test because the paper identifies it as the Torrance product improvement task. Table 2 prints negative z statistics and negative Cohen?s r values for all three dimensions, even though personalised means are higher for quality and elaboration and lower for originality. These printed signs and confidence intervals are retained unchanged; direction fields follow the stated condition results. No effect sizes have been calculated or sign-converted. The table reports no paired-difference SD, within-person outcome correlation or SE. The study is one sample with two repeated AI conditions, not two studies or independent groups. No reuse of participants from another paper is stated. No research data or analysis-code repository is identified; the GitHub link on PDF p. 5 is the Mr. Ranedeer intervention tool, not a study data/code release.
